# Prepared Palomar submission snapshot: authors, maintainer, license, and source credit.
# AGPL-3.0 is the identifier emitted by the pinned Palomar license detector;
# the project grant is GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 only.
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mathlib-initiative/formalization.yaml/99c678e569c7c4c0772db297c5ddd5e4c9b6322e/schema/v0.4.schema.json
version: "v0.4"

project:
  name: "The Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower conjecture"
  description: >-
    A Lean formalization of the main vector bound, the explicit set-family
    bound, and the no-prefactor conjecture in Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi
    sunflower conjecture by Matija Bucić, Fankang He, and Hyunwoo Lee
    (arXiv:2610.26686). The complete proof development
    uses Mathlib and contains no unresolved proof holes or nonstandard axioms.
  authors:
    - "Matija Bucić"
    - "Fankang He"
    - "Hyunwoo Lee"
  license: "AGPL-3.0"
  responsible_maintainers:
    - "Matija Bucić"

classification:
  arxiv: ["math.CO"]
  msc2020: ["05D05", "05D40"]

sources:
  - title: "Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture"
    authors:
      - "Matija Bucić"
      - "Fankang He"
      - "Hyunwoo Lee"
    id: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26686v1"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26686"
    doi: "10.48550/arXiv.2610.26686"
    supplied_pdf_sha256: "c127b9a031b600d7fef000fc09ed21ea724ff82aa70d7d3c70f72a7d9c141ea7"
    type: "paper"
    location: "Theorems 1 and 2; the conjecture consequence following Theorem 1; Sections 3 and 4"
    relationship: "formalizes"
    note: >-
      The user identified arXiv:2610.26686 as the paper supplied for this
      formalization. The arXiv record lists v1, submitted on 2026-10-19.
      The exact 16-page attachment received and reviewed on 2026-10-20 is
      separately identified by supplied_pdf_sha256; its bytes have not been
      compared with the public arXiv PDF. The paper is not redistributed.
      Formalization authors match the source authors at the user's direction.
      The submission snapshot names Matija Bucić as responsible maintainer;
      no new human review is claimed.
      The arXiv record declares its non-exclusive distribution license;
      applying AGPL-3.0 to the original project files does not relicense the paper.
    license: "https://arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/"

related_formalizations: []

status:
  scope: >-
    Theorems 1 and 2 are proved with their stated constants and ordinary
    distinct-member sunflower definitions. The vector theorem also covers
    dimension zero. The usual conjecture is proved with one constant c_k
    satisfying 0 < c_k < 2 uniformly for all N >= k - 1. The local
    interpolation, common-space dimension argument, tensorization, counting,
    vector-to-set reduction, numerical estimates, and prefactor absorption
    are all proved. The introductory literature assertions, Section 5
    applications and connections, unpublished induced Erdős–Sauer reduction,
    and novelty claims are outside the certified scope.
  sorry_count: 0
  sorry_in_definitions: 0
  axioms: ["propext", "Classical.choice", "Quot.sound"]
  main_results:
    - declaration: "ErdosSzemeredi.vector_bound"
      file: "Solution.lean"
      sorry_count: 0
      axioms: ["propext", "Classical.choice", "Quot.sound"]
      comparator_config: "comparator.json"
    - declaration: "ErdosSzemeredi.set_bound"
      file: "Solution.lean"
      sorry_count: 0
      axioms: ["propext", "Classical.choice", "Quot.sound"]
      comparator_config: "comparator.json"
    - declaration: "ErdosSzemeredi.sunflower_conjecture"
      file: "Solution.lean"
      sorry_count: 0
      axioms: ["propext", "Classical.choice", "Quot.sound"]
      comparator_config: "comparator.json"

automation:
  methods:
    - method: "agent"
      models: ["GPT-6 Astra Pro"]
      framework: "ChatGPT with collaborative agents and terminal tools"
      tool_setup: >-
        The supplied PDF was extracted and audited; collaborating agents
        developed Lean modules and reviewed statement fidelity. Lean
        4.35.0-rc2 with pinned Mathlib was used for elaboration. The exported
        dependencies of all three Solution declarations were separately
        checked with leanchecker, strict NanoDa, and con-ron in verified mode.
      cost:
        wall_time: "not tracked as a reproducible measure"
        spend_usd: "not tracked"
        hardware: "hosted Linux execution environment; hardware allocation not recorded"
      prompting_notes: >-
        The user requested verification of the supplied proof in Lean and
        preparation for Palomar. Work was divided into the environment,
        interpolation and proof audit, counting and estimates, and reduction
        and submission requirements. Proof holes and extra mathematical
        assumptions were not accepted in the Solution development.
  spend_usd: "not tracked"
  notes: >-
    Generated code and review are disclosed as automated assistance. The
    user specified Matija Bucić, Fankang He, and Hyunwoo Lee as formalization
    authors; this attribution was recorded on 2026-10-21. The user selected
    AGPL version 3 and identified arXiv:2610.26686 as the mathematical source
    on the same date. The submission snapshot names Matija Bucić as responsible
    maintainer. No external submission, publication, or author contact was
    performed during preparation.

fidelity:
  divergences: >-
    Fin D and Fin N replace the manuscript's labeled finite sets. The vector
    bound additionally allows n = 0. Its factor (4 k^2)^(1/(k-1)) is proved
    equal to the manuscript's (2k)^(2/(k-1)). A finite weighted enumerator
    proves the required counting estimate in place of a probabilistic
    Chernoff presentation. Finite permutation double counting implements
    random-block averaging. The zero-block case of Proposition 8 is
    explicit. In local interpolation the redundant repeated-prefix branch
    is omitted because the previous remainder already vanishes there. None
    of these changes weakens the main target statements.

review:
  status: "agent-reviewed; independently kernel-checked"
  reviewers: []
  notes: >-
    Mathematical and definition audits found no substantive gap in the main
    proof. Three theorem headers and six definition bodies match between
    Challenge and the implementation after whitespace normalization. A
    fresh export of the final three Solution declarations was accepted by
    leanchecker, strict NanoDa, and verified con-ron, with only propext,
    Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Original logs and hashes are retained.
    NanoDa also emitted a pretty-printer-only warning while reporting zero
    typechecker errors. The full sandboxed Palomar Comparator could not
    run because the host refused bubblewrap's proc mount; this is a separate
    outstanding verification. No human peer review, Palomar registration,
    or registry endorsement is claimed.

alignment:
  namespace: "ErdosSzemeredi"
  statements:
    - source: "Theorem 2"
      lean: "ErdosSzemeredi.vector_bound"
      module: "Solution"
      status: "proved"
      note: "Exact constant; additionally covers zero coordinates. See Sunflower.vectorBase_eq_manuscript."
    - source: "Theorem 1"
      lean: "ErdosSzemeredi.set_bound"
      module: "Solution"
      status: "proved"
      note: "For k >= 3 and N >= 1, cardinality is at most 3 times (2 - 1/(16 k^3))^N."
    - source: "Conjecture consequence following Theorem 1"
      lean: "ErdosSzemeredi.sunflower_conjecture"
      module: "Solution"
      status: "proved"
      note: "One 0 < c_k < 2 for every N >= k - 1; no prefactor."

acknowledgements: >-
  The mathematical source is Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture
  by Matija Bucić, Fankang He, and Hyunwoo Lee, arXiv:2610.26686
  (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26686; DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2610.26686).
  The development uses Lean and Mathlib and was separately checked using
  leanchecker, NanoDa, and con-ron. Palomar's public template and tooling
  informed the submission layout. The vendored formalization.yaml schema
  retains its upstream Apache-2.0 license.
